items.headline: WPA Day 90 Arrives — Trump Leaning Toward Signing 60-Day MOU but 'Still TBD' (Vance); Senior Officials: 'Couple of Language Points' on Nuclear/HEU Remain; Deal Architecture Agreed at Framework Level; No Signed Deal as of Filing
items.summary: The War Powers Act hard 90-day constitutional deadline arrives today (Friday May 29) without a signed deal. This is the hardest single calendar checkpoint of the conflict cycle. No emergency congressional session has been announced. No pre-deadline House floor vote has been scheduled. No White House Counsel or DOJ OLC public statement on the Day 90 legal posture has been issued. No CENTCOM repositioning or kinetic resumption signal materialized overnight. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture (invoked May 1) does not survive WPA plain-text Day 90 scrutiny — the naval blockade (Day 48), ongoing CENTCOM self-defense authority, and physical Hormuz closure are operative. Enforcement absent a court ruling (years) or congressional action (bipartisan majority unactivated) means the posture remains effectively intact near-term despite the constitutional clock arriving. VP JD Vance confirmed Thursday (May 28) that the US and Iran are 'very close' to a 60-day MOU — ceasefire extension, Hormuz reopening with mines cleared within 30 days, naval blockade eased in parallel with commercial shipping restoration, and nuclear talks kick-started on HEU disposal and enrichment limits. However, Vance stated it remains 'still TBD' whether Trump will sign, with 'a couple of language points' on the nuclear/HEU framework unresolved. Senior US officials confirmed Thursday afternoon that Trump was leaning toward signing but wants to wait 'a few more days' to ensure Iranian officials will not back away from the deal. The US side's desire for confidence on Iranian commitment — not Iran's resistance to the framework — appears to be the primary delay mechanism as of this filing. The deal 'hangs on Trump and Khamenei approval' (JPost); the Khamenei approval mechanism remains the structural wildcard given his courier-communication posture. Iran's own characterization (Al Arabiya) confirms Hormuz reopening and naval blockade termination are the deal terms, with commercial shipping resuming within one month of signing. Iran formally commits not to pursue nuclear weapons; HEU disposal and enrichment limits are the negotiating session topics. The Shamkhani 'fantasy' nuclear-control statement (May 27) enters Day 2 without Khamenei public correction or Araghchi formal walkback. The bipartisan House majority (Rep. Golden and six Republicans) for a WPA resolution remains real but unactivated. House Republican leadership has deferred the next war powers vote to early June — past the hard deadline. Senate has rejected nine WPA resolutions; no 10th has been introduced as of this filing. Multiple Senate Democrats have signaled intent to litigate — novel constitutional theory; years to resolve.
